# Express Gotchas

> Known Express (Node.js) patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [Express global compression() buffers SSE responses](compression-buffers-sse.md): app.use(compression()) zlib-buffers a text/event-stream so EventSource never sees live events; exclude the SSE path via a filter and set X-Accel-Buffering: no + Content-Encoding: identity. HIGH.
- [Rate-limiter skip() on unvalidated header presence](rate-limit-skip-header-presence.md): skip callbacks that exempt requests merely carrying auth-looking headers let unauthenticated attackers disable throttling; only skip on validated credentials, or use a separate higher-ceiling bucket. MEDIUM.
- [GET that mutates state records bogus actions from email link scanners](get-mutates-state-email-scanners.md): email security scanners (Safe Links, Mimecast, Proofpoint) prefetch every link in a message and fire the GET, so a survey/approve/unsubscribe link that writes on GET records bogus actions the instant the email is sent; make GET side-effect free and commit on POST behind Submit. HIGH.
- [A route is guarded by its mount, not by a path-prefix list](router-guard-by-mount-not-prefix.md): Express enforces nothing from a PLATFORM_ROUTES-style array or a "protected via the /x/ prefix" comment — a bare router.use() inherits no guard, and the unit test asserting isPlatformRoute('/x/y') === true stays green while the routes are open to the internet (GET leaked tenant names, POST ran record-deleting and mail-sending jobs). Guard at the mount, assert the mount rather than the helper, and find these by curling each privileged prefix unauthenticated. HIGH.
- [A per-IP rate limit throttles the whole NAT'd site, not the abusive client](rate-limit-per-ip-throttles-nat-site.md): express-rate-limit keys on IP by default, so a cap meant as "per client" belongs to the office — every machine at a customer site shares one public IP, and a 10/min cap starved a 77-agent site of command tokens after every API restart. It hides in steady state because long-lived credentials mean each client rarely calls, surfacing only in the reconnect storm after a deploy; client exponential backoff lengthens the tail rather than shortening it, since the shared bucket refills at a fixed rate while each client's delay doubles; and it is silent whenever health is reported on a separate unthrottled route, so throttled machines keep reporting "online" while their commands vanish. `trust proxy` fixes WHICH IP you read, not that IP is the wrong key. Key the tight budget on caller identity and keep a wide per-IP ceiling as the backstop. HIGH.
- [A literal route registered after its :id sibling is dead, and says 500 instead](route-literal-shadowed-by-param-route.md): Express matches in registration order, not by specificity, so `/tickets/stats` registered below `/tickets/:id` is handled as id='stats' — Postgres refuses the integer cast and the handler's catch returns a generic 500 that names neither the routing nor the stats handler. A file-splitting refactor introduces it as a pure move with no route added or deleted; `:id/sub-path` siblings coexist fine (different segment count), so only a bare literal at the same depth is shadowed; and a not-yet-rendered endpoint can 500 in production for months with no signal. On a text id column it 404s instead, reading as "not deployed". Register literals before params, pin with a supertest assertion, and run that test against the unfixed file — a generic db mock lets it pass on broken code. HIGH.
- [Choosing a guard from the request body hides it from every static check](guard-chosen-from-request-body-is-invisible.md): Express binds middleware at mount time, so a permission that depends on the body tempts a dispatcher handing off to pre-guarded sub-routers — it runs correctly while the route reads as `router.post("/", dispatcher)` with no guard, so a census/auditor/reviewer sees an unguarded endpoint and a later edit can remove the real guard with nothing looking wrong. Worse is guarding on the weaker permission and re-checking the stronger one by hand, which drops whatever else the guard does (step-up, denial records). Put the discriminator in the path, and force the body to agree with it. HIGH.
